category: cron job, heartbeat and uptime monitoring with incidents and status pages (hosted)

free_tier.stated: Free plan, $0 forever with no credit card: 200K beats a month, 50 monitors, 3 projects, a 1-minute minimum interval, a ping retention of 250, a maximum payload of 100 KB, unlimited team seats and 8 alert channels; the REST API and the MCP server are part of every plan, Free included
free_tier.notes: The unit is the beat, a measure of activity: the pricing page converts 200K beats into 23 cron jobs running every 5 minutes or 5 uptime monitors checked every minute, and bills activity instead of monitor count. The vocabulary has no beats term, so requests is the nearest. Advanced status pages, 30-second checks and overage start on Pro.

per_object_cap.stated: 100 KB maximum payload per ping on Free, against 1 MB on Pro

retention.stated: a ping retention of 250 on Free, against 1,000 on Pro, printed without a unit

egress.terms: not applicable: an inbound ping receiver and outbound uptime checker; monitors, incidents and channels are read through the REST API

interface_detail: A Ping API at api.drumbeats.io/v1/ping/MONITOR-ID takes plain HTTP requests with no key, the monitor ID being the credential; a REST API for monitors, incidents, projects, notification channels and groups takes an X-API-Key header; an MCP server connects Claude, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP clients.
tooling: curl or any HTTP client against the Ping API and the REST API, integration guides for common stacks, an MCP server and the web app
chaining: Dead man's switch for the scheduled jobs of free hosts with one curl at the end of a job, plus 1-minute uptime checks and a public page for every monitor.

limits.value: 200K beats per month, 50 monitors and 3 projects on Free
1-minute minimum interval on Free, 30 seconds on Pro

limits_note: A Free project gets a public page for every monitor; advanced status pages are not part of Free.
binding_note: The 200K monthly beats are reached before the 50-monitor cap by checks that run every minute, so activity binds before monitor count.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up page states no credit card is required and asks for an email address and a password of at least 8 characters, then emails a one-time verification code; Google and other sign-in options appear under Or continue with.

reliability_note: what happens past 200K beats on Free is unverified: the pricing page states only that overage starts on Pro
confidence_note: Plan limits, the API surface and the sign-up form are quoted from first-party pages. No account was opened, so the behaviour past the monthly beats is unverified: behind a sign-up.
